ud7.7:0.2: The Discourse about the Destruction of Diversification
ud7.7:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud7.7:1.3: Then at that time the Fortunate One was sitting reflecting on his own giving up of signs of conceptual diversification. Then the Fortunate One, having understood his own giving up of signs of conceptual diversification,
ud7.7:2.1: on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud7.7:3.1: “He for whom there is no diversification and persistance,
ud7.7:3.2: Who has transcended the tether and the obstacle,
ud7.7:3.3: The sage who lives without craving,
ud7.7:3.4: Is not despised by the world and its devas.”
